About KHIPU 2027 What it is: KHIPU AI ( khipu.ai ) is a non-profit organization dedicated to advancing AI talent, research, and community across Latin America. Alongside year-round regional initiatives, we host a biennial in-person gathering rotating across the continent, previously in Uruguay (2019, 2023) and Chile (2025). Next Edition: April 5–9, 2027, in São Paulo, Brazil, hosted at the Universidade de São Paulo (USP), one of Latin America's leading research universities. Watch our 2-minute video: piped.video/watch?v=Db19zoqu… (hear directly from past speakers, including Nando, and Latin American students on how KHIPU grew from a single gathering into a regional AI movement). Who Attends & Why Support - Engaging with the region's top talent and lab leaders: We bring together around 500 participants, including leading faculty and lab directors from across Latin America alongside a curated cohort of ~300 graduate students and industry researchers selected from over 1,000 applicants. As the local AI ecosystem grows rapidly, KHIPU offers a rare opportunity to engage directly with these emerging researchers and regional leaders in one place, helping shape research priorities and the safety mindset across Latin America while connecting with talent and perspectives outside Silicon Valley. 100% free attendance & student grants: Attendance is completely free for all selected students, professors, and researchers. Sponsorship funding goes directly toward travel and accommodation grants for students and faculty across Latin America who otherwise could not afford to attend. Introducing DeepRSI, a new industry standard for measuring recursive self-improvement. On preexisting benchmarks, tasks are contributor-based and short-horizon (~12 hrs). In DeepRSI, we push agents to work 48 hours on ML tasks actually derived from ongoing proprietary research. Video

We’re sharing new results showing that frontier AI models are able to outperform human experts on financial predictions for the first time. We built an environment for the challenging task of Earnings Predictions, finding that the most recent frontier models (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Astra) with Samaya’s harness, meaningfully outperform expert consensus predictions on commonly reported earnings metrics such as company revenue, gross margin and more. We built this environment to have a “point-in-time” gate in the harness to ensure no information leakage, and created financial retrieval and data tools that would respect this gate and give the models access to the same information available to experts. We also adjusted for bias in expert consensus to create a hard, bias-corrected baseline, where outperformance has real signal. Only the most recent frontier AI models are able to beat this hard baseline, pointing to an important inflection point in AI capabilities in finance. Like with FrontierFinance, we see substantial headroom for further RL training in this environment — the models show large variations in error across different rollouts. We’re continuing research on using earnings prediction and other predictive tasks to post-train models to learn from their mistakes. Get in touch if you’d like to collaborate or try out an alpha version. Link to the full research below. Video

Much of the valuable information in agent traces isn’t directly filterable with existing techniques like full text search or metadata filtering. AI Search in LangSmith closes that gap. You describe what you're looking for in plain natural language and can issue queries like "user frustrated" and "pii leaked" on the fly, which was previously impossible to do without defining an online evaluator ahead of time. LangChain (@LangChain) 🔎 Announced at Interrupt: AI Search in LangSmith You used to need an evaluator or read hours of conversations to find traces that answer questions such as: 💬 Does the user seemed frustrated?" 💬 Where did the agent fail to complete the task? 💬 Where is the user trying to cancel their subscription? Now, just describe it. LangSmith returns the traces where it happened. langchain.com/blog/agent-tra… Video — https://nitter.kareem.one/LangChain/status/2110021742169047187#m

router lives in the harness, not a gateway, bc the harness knows the task blog: langchain.com/blog/how-to-bu… Link How to Build a Model Router in the Harness How we built a model router into Open SWE's harness that cut median cost per coding task by 64% with no measurable drop in quality, and how to build your own. langchain.com NeilXbt (@neil_xbt) LangChain gave its coding agent three models and a router. Open SWE, their open-source coding agent, now sends each thread to the cheapest model likely to finish the job. they tested it on 973 threads, half routed and half always on GPT-6 Astra. median cost per thread: $0.94 against $2.61. that's 64% lower. threads ending in a merged PR: 29.2% routed, 27.3% on Astra. LangChain's p-value for that gap is 0.49. the router sent 56% of threads to the balanced model, 34% to the fast one and 10% to the performance one. they also tried always using the fast model. that test ended within a day, because engineers reported low output quality. LangChain's own caveats: the control was the most expensive model, and the router is a proof of concept. Which three models would you put in the tiers? — https://nitter.kareem.one/neil_xbt/status/2109979966859510156#m

Data brokers are now buying up SaaS data sets for anywhere from $100K to $2M SaaS are struggling now and some extra money to fill the gap by declining revenues is nice That data is then re-sold to AI training companies and AI frontier labs for the exact purpose of integrating whatever that SaaS did into the AI frontier lab's app Pretty obvious to see where this is going Franz Bruckhoff (@franzbruckhoff) Chiming in on @levelsio 's discussion about SaaS dying. A major reason increasingly more businesses will create their own software instead of paying for SaaS is that they don't want to become someone else's unpaid data source. As Greg points out, dying SaaS companies are immensely valuable data troves for AI companies. Great for them, but not great for their customers. As time goes by, "data value awareness" is going to rise I think, and more people and business will begin to see the data they produce as an asset worth something. There is an M&A company that had suggested that @taptanium 's legacy app codebases (a form of training data) could be worth ~$45k per app, just because they predate the AI revolution and contain highly complex, handwritten and correct concurrency logic that is like digital gold for AI. The value of data is widely underrated. When I was driving a Model 3 back then in Germany, my car was collecting valuable data for Tesla, which they used to develop FSD, a technology potentially worth trillions. Owners didn't get paid for that data ofc, and were actually asked to pay up in order to benefit from it fully. None of my Tesla friends thought about it and just paid, on top of delivering tons of data for it. They had no data value awareness. Some time ago Taptanium was using Appfigures to see sales, revenue, downloads and rankings in a cleaner dashboard. It was cool, but I realized I was feeding the beast with my data, which such companies also use to build App Store intelligence tools so other competitors could more easily find out what's worth cloning or attacking. So data value awareness is going to be really important, especially now that AI agents can leverage the slightest traces of cues in ways that can work for you, or against you. What kind of data do you own that might be valuable for AI training or that is strategically important to keep to yourself? And are you letting others suck it all up for free or for pennies, or is there a way you can protect it or sell it at its fair market value? — https://nitter.kareem.one/franzbruckhoff/status/2110668860948951093#m

processed.summary: Aujourd'hui, le monde de l'IA est marqué par des annonces importantes dans le développement de modèles avancés, notamment chez Mistral AI. On note aussi une forte réflexion sur l'avenir du travail à l'ère de l'IA, avec des débats sur l'automatisation et la nécessité de s'adapter rapidement aux évolutions. Enfin, des initiatives visent à démocratiser l'accès à l'IA en Afrique et en Amérique du Sud, soulignant l'importance de la formation et de la recherche pour tous.

glossaire.definition: Modèles d'IA extrêmement avancés, souvent à la pointe de la recherche et du développement.
Intelligence Artificielle Générale, une IA hypothétique capable de comprendre, apprendre et appliquer ses connaissances à n'importe quelle tâche intellectuelle humaine.
Développement d'IA qui respecte la souveraineté numérique et les réglementations d'un pays ou d'une région.
Un test standardisé utilisé pour comparer les performances de différents systèmes d'IA.
L'instruction ou la question que l'on donne à une IA pour obtenir une réponse.
Large Language Model (Grand Modèle de Langage), un type d'IA entraîné sur d'énormes quantités de texte pour comprendre et générer du langage humain.

category_summaries.actu: Mistral AI continue de marquer son territoire avec des annonces de recrutement et des développements de modèles, tandis que des initiatives comme Khipu AI et DeepIndaba travaillent à la démocratisation de l'IA dans les régions émergentes. On observe également des avancées dans la capacité des IA à surpasser les experts humains dans des domaines comme la finance.
category_summaries.tips: Des conseils pratiques émergent concernant l'utilisation d'agents IA dans le cadre professionnel, notamment pour optimiser les coûts et l'efficacité. L'importance de la gestion des données et de la compréhension des mécanismes de l'IA pour rester pertinent face aux évolutions rapides est également soulignée.
category_summaries.idees: La discussion porte sur l'impact sociétal de l'IA, notamment l'automatisation du travail et l'idée que le capitalisme pourrait s'auto-consommer face à ces avancées. La réflexion porte aussi sur la valeur des données dans l'écosystème de l'IA et la nécessité d'une prise de conscience pour les utilisateurs et les entreprises.
category_summaries.outils: De nouveaux outils et approches apparaissent, comme DeepRSI pour mesurer l'auto-amélioration des IA, LangChain qui se positionne comme une plateforme clé pour assembler des modèles spécialisés, et des avancées dans la recherche d'informations au sein des traces d'agents IA.

actu.text_fr: Des modèles d'IA de pointe ont désormais la capacité de surpasser les experts humains dans les prédictions financières. actu.text_original: We’re sharing new results showing that frontier AI models are able to outperform human experts on financial predictions for the first time. We built an environment for the challenging task of Earnings Predictions, finding that the most recent frontier models (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Astra) with Samaya’s harness, meaningfully outperform expert consensus predictions on commonly reported earnings metrics such as company revenue, gross margin and more. We built this environment to have a “point-in-time” gate in the harness to ensure no information leakage, and created financial retrieval and data tools that would respect this gate and give the models access to the same information available to experts. We also adjusted for bias in expert consensus to create a hard, bias-corrected baseline, where outperformance has real signal. Only the most recent frontier AI models are able to beat this hard baseline, pointing to an important inflection point in AI capabilities in finance. Like with FrontierFinance, we see substantial headroom for further RL training in this environment — the models show large variations in error across different rollouts. We’re continuing research on using earnings prediction and other predictive tasks to post-train models to learn from their mistakes. LangChain's p-value for that gap is 0.49. the router sent 56% of threads to the balanced model, 34% to the fast one and 10% to the performance one. they also tried always using the fast model. that test ended within a day, because engineers reported low output quality. LangChain's own caveats: the control was the most expensive model, and the router is a proof of concept. Which three models would you put in the tiers? — https://nitter.kareem.one/neil_xbt/status/2109979966859510156#m

idees.text_fr: Pieter Levels souligne que les données générées par les logiciels (SaaS) sont de plus en plus achetées entre 100 000 $ et 2 M$ par des courtiers, pour être ensuite revendues aux entreprises d'IA. Il alerte sur le fait que les données que nous produisons peuvent avoir une grande valeur et que les entreprises devraient être plus conscientes de cette valeur pour mieux la protéger ou la monétiser, au lieu de la laisser être utilisée gratuitement par les IA.
idees.text_original: Data brokers are now buying up SaaS data sets for anywhere from $100K to $2M SaaS are struggling now and some extra money to fill the gap by declining revenues is nice That data is then re-sold to AI training companies and AI frontier labs for the exact purpose of integrating whatever that SaaS did into the AI frontier lab's app Pretty obvious to see where this is going Franz Bruckhoff (@franzbruckhoff) Chiming in on @levelsio 's discussion about SaaS dying. A major reason increasingly more businesses will create their own software instead of paying for SaaS is that they don't want to become someone else's unpaid data source. As Greg points out, dying SaaS companies are immensely valuable data troves for AI companies. Great for them, but not great for their customers. As time goes by, "data value awareness" is going to rise I think, and more people and business will begin to see the data they produce as an asset worth something. There is an M&A company that had suggested that @taptanium 's legacy app codebases (a form of training data) could be worth ~$45k per app, just because they predate the AI revolution and contain highly complex, handwritten and correct concurrency logic that is like digital gold for AI. The value of data is widely underrated. When I was driving a Model 3 back then in Germany, my car was collecting valuable data for Tesla, which they used to develop FSD, a technology potentially worth trillions. Owners didn't get paid for that data ofc, and were actually asked to pay up in order to benefit from it fully. None of my Tesla friends thought about it and just paid, on top of delivering tons of data for it. They had no data value awareness. Some time ago Taptanium was using Appfigures to see sales, revenue, downloads and rankings in a cleaner dashboard. It was cool, but I realized I was feeding the beast with my data, which such companies also use to build App Store intelligence tools so other competitors could more easily find out what's worth cloning or attacking. So data value awareness is going to be really important, especially now that AI agents can leverage the slightest traces of cues in ways that can work for you, or against you. What kind of data do you own that might be valuable for AI training or that is strategically important to keep to yourself? And are you letting others suck it all up for free or for pennies, or is there a way you can sell it at its fair market value? — https://nitter.kareem.one/franzbruckhoff/status/2110668860948951093#m
idees.decryptage: Les entreprises d'IA achètent des données d'utilisation de logiciels (SaaS) pour entraîner leurs modèles. Pieter Levels nous met en garde sur la valeur de nos propres données et nous invite à y réfléchir avant de les laisser utiliser gratuitement.

Il pense que cela résoudra les problèmes de qualité rencontrés depuis le COVID, liés aux pénuries de main-d'œuvre et aux aides sociales.

outils.text_fr: Jeff Dean annonce DeepRSI, une nouvelle méthode pour mesurer comment les IA s'améliorent seules. Cette approche pousse les IA à travailler plus longtemps (48h) sur des tâches réelles, offrant une évaluation plus réaliste de leurs capacités d'apprentissage continu par rapport aux méthodes traditionnelles plus courtes.
outils.text_original: Introducing DeepRSI, a new industry standard for measuring recursive self-improvement. On preexisting benchmarks, tasks are contributor-based and short-horizon (~12 hrs). In DeepRSI, we push agents to work 48 hours on ML tasks actually derived from ongoing proprietary research. Video
outils.decryptage: DeepRSI est une nouvelle façon de tester les IA pour voir à quel point elles peuvent s'améliorer seules sur des tâches difficiles, en les faisant travailler plus longtemps que d'habitude.

outils.text_fr: Des modèles d'IA de pointe ont désormais la capacité de surpasser les experts humains dans les prédictions financières. En utilisant des données financières et en respectant des contraintes temporelles strictes, des modèles comme Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 et Astra montrent une performance supérieure aux consensus d'experts.
outils.text_original: We’re sharing new results showing that frontier AI models are able to outperform human experts on financial predictions for the first time. We built an environment for the challenging task of Earnings Predictions, finding that the most recent frontier models (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Astra) with Samaya’s harness, meaningfully outperform expert consensus predictions on commonly reported earnings metrics such as company revenue, gross margin and more. We built this environment to have a “point-in-time” gate in the harness to ensure no information leakage, and created financial retrieval and data tools that would respect this gate and give the models access to the same information available to experts. We also adjusted for bias in expert consensus to create a hard, bias-corrected baseline, where outperformance has real signal. Only the most recent frontier AI models are able to beat this hard baseline, pointing to an important inflection point in AI capabilities in finance. Like with FrontierFinance, we see substantial headroom for further RL training in this environment — the models show large variations in error across different rollouts. We’re continuing research on using earnings prediction and other predictive tasks to post-train models to learn from their mistakes. Get in touch if you’d like to collaborate or try out an alpha version. Link to the full research below. Video
outils.decryptage: Des IA très avancées peuvent maintenant faire de meilleures prédictions financières que les experts humains, ce qui marque un tournant important dans leur utilisation pour la finance.

outils.text_fr: Harrison Chase met en avant LangChain comme un leader potentiel pour assembler différents modèles d'IA. Il explique que LangChain est idéal pour connecter des modèles spécialisés, y compris les nouveaux 'constrained decision models' (CDMs), qui sont efficaces pour des tâches précises comme la résumé ou l'extraction d'informations.
outils.text_original: As I’ve been saying, LangChain is going to be the leader in composable AI because their tech is perfect for stitching together all of these smaller specialized models. And now we have another category of models to work with: CDMs. Perfect for things like compaction and extracting useful data from context. Sydney Runkle (@sydneyrunkle) we're excited to partner with @scaledown_team to offer support for their new constrained decision models (CDMs) in @LangChain ! these cheap+fast models are tailored to specific critical tasks in the agent loop, like summarization, extraction, and classification. — https://nitter.kareem.one/sydneyrunkle/status/2109979165437116723#m
outils.decryptage: LangChain est une plateforme qui aide à connecter différents outils d'IA spécialisés. Elle intègre maintenant les CDMs, des modèles d'IA très efficaces pour des tâches spécifiques comme résumer des textes ou extraire des informations précises.

outils.text_fr: Harrison Chase présente la nouvelle fonctionnalité 'AI Search' dans LangSmith. Cet outil permet de rechercher des informations dans les traces d'utilisation des agents IA en langage naturel, par exemple, pour trouver des moments où un utilisateur était frustré ou si des données personnelles ont fuité, sans avoir à définir des critères de recherche complexes à l'avance.
outils.text_original: Much of the valuable information in agent traces isn’t directly filterable with existing techniques like full text search or metadata filtering. AI Search in LangSmith closes that gap. You describe what you're looking for in plain natural language and can issue queries like "user frustrated" and "pii leaked" on the fly, which was previously impossible to do without defining an online evaluator ahead of time. LangChain (@LangChain) 🔎 Announced at Interrupt: AI Search in LangSmith You used to need an evaluator or read hours of conversations to find traces that answer questions such as: 💬 Does the user seemed frustrated?" 💬 Where did the agent fail to complete the task? 💬 Where is the user trying to cancel their subscription? Now, just describe it. LangSmith returns the traces where it happened. langchain.com/blog/agent-tra… Video — https://nitter.kareem.one/LangChain/status/2110021742169047187#m
outils.decryptage: AI Search dans LangSmith permet de rechercher facilement des informations spécifiques dans les conversations des IA en utilisant des phrases simples, ce qui était auparavant très compliqué.

outils.text_fr: Harrison Chase explique comment utiliser un 'routeur de modèles' dans LangChain pour optimiser les coûts. En dirigeant chaque tâche vers le modèle IA le plus adapté et le moins cher, il a été possible de réduire le coût moyen par tâche de 64% sans perte de qualité notable.
outils.text_original: router lives in the harness, not a gateway, bc the harness knows the task blog: langchain.com/blog/how-to-bu… Link How to Build a Model Router in the Harness How we built a model router into Open SWE's harness that cut median cost per coding task by 64% with no measurable drop in quality, and how to build your own. langchain.com NeilXbt (@neil_xbt) LangChain gave its coding agent three models and a router. Open SWE, their open-source coding agent, now sends each thread to the cheapest model likely to finish the job. they tested it on 973 threads, half routed and half always on GPT-6 Astra. median cost per thread: $0.94 against $2.61. that's 64% lower. threads ending in a merged PR: 29.2% routed, 27.3% on Astra. LangChain's p-value for that gap is 0.49. the router sent 56% of threads to the balanced model, 34% to the fast one and 10% to the performance one. they also tried always using the fast model. that test ended within a day, because engineers reported low output quality. LangChain's own caveats: the control was the most expensive model, and the router is a proof of concept. Which three models would you put in the tiers? — https://nitter.kareem.one/neil_xbt/status/2109979966859510156#m
outils.decryptage: Pour réduire les coûts, on peut utiliser un système (router) qui choisit le modèle d'IA le plus économique pour chaque tâche, comme démontré avec LangChain, permettant d'économiser jusqu'à 64% sans sacrifier la qualité.

outils.text_fr: Arthur Mensch annonce que le modèle Mistral Large 4 a été intégré au benchmark sudo L7, qui évalue les capacités des IA dans des tâches d'ingénierie logicielle complexes. Mistral Large 4 obtient un score de 13.3%, surpassant d'autres modèles comme Muse Spark et Grok.
outils.text_original: 🇫🇷 Le Chonk joins the sudo L7 leaderboard 🇫🇷 We just added @MistralAI 's Mistral Large 4 to sudo L7, our benchmark for staff-level software engineering. Mistral Large 4 scores 13.3%, ahead of Muse Spark 1.3 (12.2%) and Grok 4.7 (10.6%). sudo L7 tests whether coding agents can go beyond writing correct code to exercise the judgment of experienced engineers: navigating messy systems, spotting hidden risks, and knowing when technically correct code is still the wrong thing to ship. Allez, le Chonk ! 🥖 Leaderboard ↓ surgehq.ai/benchmarks/sudo-l…
